subject: Materials Science
title: Optical Properties: Color and Transparency
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Optical Properties: Color and Transparency.

hook.text: Glass is transparent. Metals are shiny. Wood is opaque and brown. Why do materials look so different?

buildup.text: When light hits a material, it's absorbed, reflected, or transmitted — the balance defines appearance.

discovery.text: Metals reflect because free electrons absorb and re-emit light instantly — that's the metallic luster.

twist.text: Gold reflects red and yellow but absorbs blue — that's why it's golden, not silver.

climax.text: Fiber optic cables transmit light for 100 km with minimal loss — ultra-pure glass at its finest.

punchline.text: A material's appearance is just how its electrons interact with light.

quiz.question: Why do metals appear shiny?
options: Free electrons absorb and re-emit light, creating reflection
They transmit all light without absorption
